verses.text: A man named Ananias, along with his wife Sapphira, sold some property.
He secretly kept some of the money for himself, and his wife knew about it. He brought the rest and placed it at the apostles’ feet.
Peter said, “Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart so you would lie to the Holy Spirit and keep some of the land’s money?
“Before you sold it, wasn’t it yours? And after you sold it, wasn’t the money yours to do with as you wished? Why did you plan this in your heart? You haven’t lied to people; you have lied to God.”
When Ananias heard this, he fell down and died. Great fear came over everyone who heard about it.
Some young men got up, wrapped his body, carried him out, and buried him.
About three hours later, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter asked her, “Tell me, did you sell the land for this amount?” She answered, “Yes, that was the price.”
Peter said to her, “How could the two of you agree to test the Lord’s Spirit? Listen—the people who buried your husband are at the door, and they’ll carry you out too.”
At once she fell down at his feet and died. The young men came in, found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear came over the whole church and everyone who heard about these events.
The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people. The believers met together at Solomon’s Porch.
The others didn’t dare join them, but the people spoke highly of them.
More and more believers—both men and women—were added to the Lord.
People even carried the sick into the streets and laid them on beds and mats, hoping that Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.
Crowds also came from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing sick people and those troubled by unclean spirits. They were all healed.
Then the high priest and everyone with him, who belonged to the Sadducees, stood up, filled with jealousy.
They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
But during the night, an angel of the Lord opened the jail doors, led them out, and said,
“Go stand in the temple and tell the people everything about this new life.”

They heard him and entered the temple around daybreak to teach. Meanwhile, the high priest and his associates called the council together, along with all the elders of Israel, and sent for the prisoners.
But when the officers arrived at the jail, they didn’t find the apostles there. They returned and reported,
“We found the jail securely locked and the guards standing at the doors. But when we opened them, no one was inside.”
When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this report, they were confused and wondered what would happen next.
Then someone came in and told them, “The men you put in jail are in the temple, standing there and teaching the people.”
The captain went with the officers and brought the apostles back, but without force, because they were afraid the people would stone them.
They brought the apostles in and stood them before the council. The high priest questioned them:
“We strictly ordered you not to teach in this name! And look—you’ve filled Jerusalem with your teaching and want to make us responsible for this man’s blood.”
Peter and the other apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than people.
“The God of our ancestors raised Jesus to life—the one you killed by hanging him on a tree.
“God exalted him to his right hand as Leader and Savior, to give Israel the opportunity to turn back and receive forgiveness of sins.
“We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God gives to those who obey him.”
When they heard this, the council members were furious and wanted to kill the apostles.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel stood up in the council. He was a law teacher respected by all the people. He ordered the apostles to be taken outside for a little while.
Then he said, “People of Israel, think carefully about what you’re about to do to these men.
“Some time ago Theudas appeared, claiming to be someone important. About four hundred men joined him. He was killed, and all his followers scattered and came to nothing.
“After him, Judas from Galilee appeared during the census and led some people away with him. He also died, and all his followers were scattered.
“So here’s my advice: leave these men alone. If their plan or work comes from people, it will fail.
“But if it comes from God, you won’t be able to stop them—and you might end up fighting against God.” They accepted his advice.
They called the apostles back, had them beaten, ordered them not to speak in Jesus’ name, and released them.
The apostles left the council, glad that God had counted them worthy to suffer shame for Jesus’ name.
Every day, in the temple and in people’s homes, they kept teaching and announcing that Jesus is the Messiah.
